explanation: You used a variable name that Java has never seen. The variable was not declared, or the name is misspelled.
suggestion: Declare the variable before you use it, for example: int count = 0; Check the spelling carefully.

explanation: You called a method that Java cannot find. The name may be misspelled, or the method does not exist on that object.
suggestion: Check the method name spelling. Make sure the object is the right type and that the method really exists for it.

explanation: Java cannot find the class name you used. It may be misspelled or missing an import.
suggestion: Check the class name spelling. If the class is in another package, add import package.ClassName; at the top of the file.

explanation: Java does not know the name you used (a variable, method, or class). It was never declared, is spelled wrong, or is out of reach.
suggestion: Check the spelling. Make sure you declared the variable or method before using it. If it is a class from another package, add the correct import.

explanation: You tried to put a larger or more precise number into a smaller type (for example a double into an int). Some information would be lost.
suggestion: Use a cast if you really mean to drop the extra information: int x = (int) myDouble; Or change the variable to a wider type like double.

patterns: String cannot be converted to int
incompatible types: String cannot be converted to int
explanation: You tried to use text (a String) where a whole number (int) is required. Java will not convert text to a number automatically.
suggestion: Convert the text with Integer.parseInt(myString). Make sure the text actually contains a number first.

patterns: int cannot be converted to String
incompatible types: int cannot be converted to String
explanation: You tried to use a whole number where text (a String) is required. Java will not convert a number to text automatically in this situation.
suggestion: Convert the number with String.valueOf(myInt) or by writing "" + myInt.

explanation: A method that should not return a value (void) tried to return something, or the returned value does not match what the method promised.
suggestion: If the method is void, remove the return value (use return; or just end the method). Otherwise make the returned value match the method's return type.

explanation: The value you returned does not match the type the method said it would return.
suggestion: Check the method's return type (the word before the method name). Return a value of that exact type, or change the return type if it was wrong.

explanation: A method that must return a value reaches the end without a return statement on every path.
suggestion: Add a return statement that returns the correct type. Make sure every branch (if/else) also returns a value.

explanation: You wrote two methods with the same name and the same parameter types in the same class.
suggestion: Rename one method, or change the parameters so the two methods are different (overloading). You cannot have two identical method signatures.

explanation: A class with this name already exists in the same package or file.
suggestion: Rename one of the classes, or make sure you are not compiling the same class twice.

explanation: You declared the same name twice in the same scope. Java does not allow two variables (or methods) with the same name there.
suggestion: Rename one of them, or remove the extra declaration. Each name can only be declared once in the same block.

patterns: variable .* might not have been initialized
explanation: You used a local variable before giving it a value. Java requires every local variable to be set before it is read.
suggestion: Assign a value when you declare the variable, for example: int x = 0; Or assign it in every branch before you use it.

patterns: does not override or implement a method from a supertype
method does not override or implement
explanation: You used @Override, but the method does not match any method in a parent class or interface. The name or parameters may be wrong.
suggestion: Check the method name and parameter types against the parent class. Fix the spelling or remove the @Override annotation if you did not mean to override.

patterns: cannot assign a value to final variable
cannot assign a value to final
explanation: You tried to change a variable that was marked final. Final variables can only be set once.
suggestion: Remove the final keyword if you need to change the value later. Or only assign to the variable once.

explanation: You used square brackets [] on something that is not an array.
suggestion: Only use [] on arrays. Check that the variable was declared as an array, for example: int[] nums = new int[5];

patterns: array index is out of bounds
Index .* out of bounds for length
explanation: You used an index that is too big or too small for the array. Valid indexes go from 0 to length-1.
suggestion: Check the array length with array.length. Only use indexes from 0 up to array.length - 1.

explanation: You tried to use something that is null (empty). Calling a method or reading a field on null causes this crash.
suggestion: Check that the variable is not null before you use it. Example: if (obj != null) { obj.doSomething(); }

explanation: You used an index that is outside the length of the string. Valid indexes go from 0 to length()-1.
suggestion: Check the string length with str.length(). Only use indexes from 0 up to str.length() - 1.

explanation: You divided a number by zero. Division by zero is not allowed.
suggestion: Check that the divisor is not zero before dividing. Example: if (b != 0) { result = a / b; }

explanation: You tried to turn text into a number, but the text was not a valid number.
suggestion: Make sure the string only contains digits (and an optional minus sign or decimal point). Check for empty strings or letters before parsing.

explanation: You tried to treat an object as a different type than it really is (a bad cast).
suggestion: Check the real type with instanceof before casting. Example: if (obj instanceof String) { String s = (String) obj; }

explanation: A method received an argument that it cannot accept (wrong value or wrong kind of data).
suggestion: Read the method documentation for the allowed values. Check the arguments you are passing and fix any that are out of range or the wrong type.

explanation: You called a method at a time when the object was not ready for that action.
suggestion: Check the order of your method calls. Some methods can only be used after the object has been set up or opened.

explanation: You used an index that is outside the valid range of a list or similar collection.
suggestion: Check the size with list.size(). Valid indexes go from 0 to size() - 1.

patterns: reached end of file while parsing
explanation: Java reached the end of the file but was still expecting more code, usually a missing closing brace }.
suggestion: Count your opening { and closing }. Add any missing } at the end of the class or method.

explanation: Java expected a class, interface, or enum declaration at this point. Extra code may be outside of any class.
suggestion: Make sure all methods and variables are inside a class. Move stray code inside the class body.

explanation: A semicolon is missing at the end of a statement.
suggestion: Add a semicolon (;) at the end of the line shown in the error.

explanation: A curly brace { or } is missing where Java expected one.
suggestion: Add the missing { or } so that every block is properly opened and closed.

explanation: A closing parenthesis ) is missing.
suggestion: Add the missing ) to match an opening ( on that line or the line above.

explanation: Java found a symbol or keyword in a place where it does not belong inside an expression.
suggestion: Check for extra or missing symbols, a missing semicolon on the previous line, or a keyword used in the wrong place.

explanation: Java found something unexpected where it expected a type name (like int or String).
suggestion: Check the line for typos or misplaced keywords. Make sure type names are spelled correctly.

explanation: This line is not a complete statement that Java can run. It may be just a value or an incomplete expression.
suggestion: Turn it into a full statement, for example by assigning it to a variable or calling a method. Add a semicolon if one is missing.

patterns: cannot return a value from method whose result type is void
void methods cannot return a value
explanation: A void method tried to return a value. Void means the method returns nothing.
suggestion: Remove the value after return (use return; or just end the method). Or change the method's return type if it should return something.

patterns: non-static method .* cannot be referenced from a static context
non-static variable .* cannot be referenced from a static context
cannot be referenced from a static context
explanation: You tried to use a normal (instance) variable or method from a static method (like main). Static methods do not have an object instance.
suggestion: Create an object first and call the method on it: MyClass obj = new MyClass(); obj.method(); Or make the variable/method static if it does not need an instance.

patterns: method .* in class .* cannot be applied to given types
explanation: You called a method with the wrong number or wrong types of arguments.
suggestion: Check the method parameters. Pass the exact types and count of values the method expects.

patterns: constructor .* in class .* cannot be applied to given types
constructor .* cannot be applied to given types
explanation: You called a constructor with the wrong number or wrong types of arguments.
suggestion: Check the constructor parameters in the class. Pass the exact number and types of values it expects when you write new ClassName(...).

explanation: Java could not find a constructor that matches the arguments you passed when creating an object with new.
suggestion: Check the number and types of values you pass to new ClassName(...). Look at the class to see which constructors it actually has.

explanation: Java cannot find the package you named in an import or package statement. The name may be wrong or the package is not on the classpath.
suggestion: Check the package name spelling. Make sure the library is installed and on the classpath (or added as a dependency in your project).

explanation: You tried to use a class that is not visible from your code (for example it is package-private and lives in another package).
suggestion: Make the class public if it should be used from other packages, or move your code into the same package. Check that the class file is available.

patterns: is public, should be declared in a file named
explanation: A public class must be saved in a file that has exactly the same name as the class (plus .java).
suggestion: Rename the file to match the public class name. Example: public class Hello must live in Hello.java.

explanation: You used a modifier (like public or private) in a place where Java does not allow it.
suggestion: Remove the modifier from that location. Local variables inside a method cannot be public or private.

explanation: Java found a type in a place where it expected something else (for example a value instead of a type name, or the wrong kind of type).
suggestion: Check the line carefully. You may have used a type name where a variable was needed, or the wrong type for an operator.

explanation: The whole number you wrote is larger than an int can hold. Plain numbers without a suffix are treated as int.
suggestion: Add an L at the end to make it a long: 10000000000L. Or use a smaller number that fits in an int.

explanation: A string was started with a quote but never closed on the same line.
suggestion: Add the missing closing quote ". For text that spans several lines, use text blocks (""" ... """) in newer Java, or concatenate strings.

explanation: You wrote two single quotes with nothing between them (''). A character literal must contain exactly one character.
suggestion: Put one character between the quotes, for example 'A'. If you want an empty string, use "" (double quotes) instead.

explanation: You used a backslash \ followed by a character that is not a valid escape (like \n or \t).
suggestion: Use a valid escape such as \n (newline), \t (tab), \\ (backslash), or \" (quote). To write a normal backslash in a path, double it: "C:\\folder".

explanation: A case label appears outside of a switch statement. case can only be used inside switch.
suggestion: Put the case inside a switch block, or remove it if it does not belong there.

explanation: You used break outside of a switch or a loop (for, while, do). break is only allowed in those places.
suggestion: Remove the break, or move it inside the switch or loop where you meant to exit early.

explanation: You used continue outside of a loop. continue is only allowed inside for, while, or do-while.
suggestion: Remove the continue, or move it inside the loop where you meant to skip to the next iteration.

explanation: This line of code can never run because a return, break, continue, or throw above it always leaves the block first.
suggestion: Remove the unreachable code, or change the logic above so that this line can be reached in some cases.

patterns: is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement
explanation: You wrote a catch for an exception that the try block can never throw. Java does not allow catching exceptions that cannot occur there.
suggestion: Remove that catch block, or catch a more general exception only if you really need it. Check which exceptions the code inside try actually throws.

patterns: must be caught or declared to be thrown
explanation: A method calls something that can throw a checked exception, but you neither caught it nor declared it with throws.
suggestion: Either wrap the call in try/catch, or add throws ExceptionType to the method signature. Example: public void read() throws IOException { ... }

explanation: You have two catch blocks for the same exception (or a parent exception was caught first, so the second catch can never run).
suggestion: Remove the duplicate catch, or put the more specific exception catch before the more general one.

explanation: A try block must be followed by at least one catch, a finally, or a try-with-resources declaration.
suggestion: Add a catch (Exception e) { ... } or a finally { ... } after the try block.

explanation: A catch block appears without a matching try above it.
suggestion: Put a try { ... } block before the catch, or remove the catch if it is not needed.

explanation: A finally block appears without a matching try above it.
suggestion: Put a try { ... } block before the finally, or remove the finally if it is not needed.

explanation: You tried to create an array with a negative size. Array length must be zero or a positive number.
suggestion: Check the number you pass to new Type[size]. Make sure it is not negative. Example: new int[10] is OK; new int[-1] is not.

explanation: A method kept calling itself (or a chain of methods kept calling each other) so many times that the call stack ran out of space.
suggestion: Check for infinite recursion. Make sure every recursive method has a clear stopping condition that is eventually reached.

explanation: The program tried to use more memory than the Java virtual machine can give.
suggestion: Process data in smaller pieces instead of loading everything at once. Look for large arrays or collections that grow without limit.

explanation: Java found the class at compile time but cannot find it at runtime. The class file may be missing from the classpath.
suggestion: Make sure the class file or JAR is on the classpath when you run the program. Rebuild the project and check that no class files were deleted.

explanation: Java tried to load a class by name and could not find it on the classpath.
suggestion: Check the class name spelling. Make sure the JAR or class folder is on the classpath. For drivers (like JDBC), ensure the driver JAR is included.

explanation: At runtime Java looked for a method that does not exist in the class that was actually loaded. This often means mixed versions of a library.
suggestion: Make sure all JARs are the same version you compiled against. Clean and rebuild the project so old class files are not mixed with new ones.

explanation: A class was expected to implement an abstract method, but the method is missing at runtime. This usually means incompatible library versions.
suggestion: Update or align the versions of your libraries so that implementations match the interfaces they claim to support. Clean and rebuild.

explanation: You called a method that this object does not support. Some collections (like those from Arrays.asList) do not allow add or remove.
suggestion: Use a different collection type that supports the operation, for example new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(...)) if you need to add or remove items.

explanation: You changed a collection while looping over it (for example removing an item inside a for-each loop). That is not allowed.
suggestion: Use an Iterator and call iterator.remove(), or collect the items to remove in a separate list and remove them after the loop.

explanation: A thread was interrupted while it was waiting or sleeping. This is often used to signal that the thread should stop.
suggestion: Handle InterruptedException in a catch block. Restore the interrupt flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() if you cannot stop yet.

explanation: Java could not find the file at the path you gave, or could not open it for the mode you requested.
suggestion: Check the file path spelling and that the file really exists. Use an absolute path if a relative path is unclear. Make sure you have permission to read or write it.

explanation: The program tried to read more data from a stream, but the end of the file or stream was already reached.
suggestion: Check for end of stream before reading more (for example with read() returning -1). Do not assume there is always more data.

explanation: An input or output operation failed (reading, writing, or connecting to a stream).
suggestion: Check that the file or stream is open and available. Handle the exception with try/catch and print or log the detailed message for more clues.

explanation: Java could not connect to the remote server. The server may be down, the address wrong, or a firewall may be blocking the connection.
suggestion: Check the host name and port. Make sure the server is running and reachable (try it in a browser or with ping). Check firewall settings.

explanation: A network read or connection took too long and timed out.
suggestion: Increase the timeout if the server is slow, or check that the server is responding. Handle the timeout so your program can retry or show a clear message.

explanation: Java could not resolve the host name to an IP address. The name may be misspelled or there may be no network/DNS.
suggestion: Check the host name spelling. Make sure you have internet access and that DNS is working. Try the address in a browser.

explanation: A database operation failed. The SQL may be wrong, the connection may be closed, or the database may have rejected the command.
suggestion: Read the detailed message from the exception. Check your SQL syntax, table and column names, and that the connection is open. Log e.getMessage() for more detail.

explanation: Java could not find a method that matches the name and argument types you used in the call.
suggestion: Check the method name spelling and the number and types of arguments. Look at the class to see which methods are available.

explanation: Java found more than one method or variable with that name and cannot decide which one you mean.
suggestion: Use a more specific name, cast the argument to the exact type you want, or call the method on a clearly typed variable.

patterns: static method .* cannot be referenced from a non-static context
cannot be referenced from a non-static context
explanation: You tried to use a static method in a way that Java does not allow in this context (rare wording).
suggestion: Call static methods with the class name: ClassName.method(). Make sure you are not mixing static and instance usage incorrectly.

explanation: You tried to use the result of a void method as a value. Void methods return nothing.
suggestion: Do not assign a void method call to a variable. Call it as a statement on its own line: myMethod();

explanation: An opening parenthesis ( is missing where Java expected one.
suggestion: Add the missing ( in the method call or expression on that line.

explanation: A closing square bracket ] is missing.
suggestion: Add the missing ] to close an array index or array declaration.

explanation: The source file contains a character that is not allowed in Java code (sometimes copied from a website or another language).
suggestion: Delete the bad character and type it again. Watch for fancy quotes, special symbols, or hidden characters.

explanation: The decimal number you wrote is larger than the float or double type can hold.
suggestion: Use a smaller number, or check that you did not add too many digits. For very large values consider BigDecimal.

explanation: You declared or created an array but left out the size in the brackets.
suggestion: Provide the size: new int[10]. Or when declaring with values: int[] a = {1, 2, 3};

patterns: final parameter .* may not be assigned
explanation: You tried to change a method parameter that was marked final. Final parameters cannot be reassigned.
suggestion: Remove the final keyword from the parameter if you need to change it, or use a new local variable instead.

explanation: Two methods have the same name and, after generics are removed, the same parameter types. Java cannot tell them apart at runtime.
suggestion: Rename one of the methods, or change the parameters so they are different even without generics (for example use different raw types).

patterns: type parameter .* is not within its bound
explanation: You used a type argument that does not satisfy the bounds declared for that type parameter (for example T extends Number but you passed String).
suggestion: Pass a type that matches the bound. Check the class or method declaration for extends or super constraints.

explanation: Java tried to guess a generic type but the constraints conflict (the type would need to be two incompatible things at once).
suggestion: Add an explicit type argument, for example Collections.<String>emptyList(), or adjust the variables so the types agree.
